standard_prerequisites.name: Numerical intersection numbers via Euler characteristics of tensor powers
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Varieties, section on numerical intersections (definition of (L_1 ... L_d . Z))
standard_prerequisites.use: The intersection number is defined through the coefficient of a Hilbert polynomial; the proof works directly in these terms.

core_obligations: Reduce to the case X = Z and L_1 = O_X(D) by replacing X with Z and restricting the L_i (proof lines 10554-10555).
Write the short exact sequence 0 -> L_1^{otimes -1} -> O_X -> O_D -> 0 coming from D as the zero locus ideal sheaf (proof lines 10556-10560).

Define the Hilbert polynomials P(n_1,...,n_d) and Q(n_1,...,n_d) and derive the difference identity P(n_1,...) - P(n_1 - 1, n_2, ...) = Q from additivity of Euler characteristics (proof lines 10561-10573).

Compare coefficients of n_1 ... n_d: since the total degree of P is at most d, this coefficient equals the coefficient of n_2 ... n_d in Q, which is exactly the numerical intersection identity (proof lines 10574-10576).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to X = Z with L_1 = O_X(D).
Use the zero-locus short exact sequence for D.
Translate both sides into Hilbert polynomials and subtract shifted arguments.
Compare leading coefficients to conclude the numerical intersection equality.
difficulty_reason: The lemma reduces a numerical intersection number (L_1 ... L_d . Z) on a proper d-dimensional closed subscheme Z to the divisor intersection (L_2 ... L_d . D), assuming L_1|_Z is the invertible sheaf O_Z(D) of an effective Cartier divisor D. The proof replaces X by Z, uses the short exact sequence 0 -> L_1^{-1} -> O_X -> O_D -> 0, expresses both sides through the Hilbert polynomials P and Q of the L_i, and shows P - P(shifted) = Q; the coefficient comparison uses that the total degree of P is at most d (proof lines 10554-10576). H2: the polynomial-difference translation and the coefficient argument are the non-routine steps.
